title: El Conde Lucanor
author: Don Juan Manuel
sourceEdition: Three exemplos (V, XXXII, XXXV) from El Conde Lucanor (1335), retold in modern Spanish

premise.en: Whenever Count Lucanor faces a difficult decision, his wise advisor Patronio answers with a short story that quietly holds the lesson he needs.
premise.es: Cada vez que el Conde Lucanor enfrenta una decisión difícil, su sabio consejero Patronio le responde con un cuento breve que contiene, en silencio, la lección que necesita.

summary.en: In medieval Spain, Count Lucanor regularly asks his advisor Patronio for guidance on the problems that trouble him. Patronio never answers directly; instead, he tells a story about someone who once faced a similar situation, and lets the count draw his own conclusion from it.
summary.es: En la España medieval, el Conde Lucanor le pide con frecuencia consejo a su asesor Patronio sobre los problemas que lo preocupan. Patronio nunca responde de manera directa; en cambio, cuenta una historia sobre alguien que vivió una situación parecida, y deja que el conde saque su propia conclusión.

tutorNotes.pronunciation: Practice the trilled r in «zorra» and «burladores», and the c before e/i pronounced as [s] in Latin American Spanish, as in «pedazo», «paño» and «príncipe».
tutorNotes.grammar: Each frame story uses fixed formulas in pretérito («le dijo», «respondió Patronio») around retellings that lean on imperfecto for background description; watch for simple «para que» clauses expressing purpose, one of the few subjunctive uses appropriate at this level.
tutorNotes.culture: Don Juan Manuel wrote El Conde Lucanor around 1335, making it one of the earliest and most influential works of Spanish prose fiction; its frame structure, where an advisor answers with a moral tale, shaped storytelling traditions across Europe for centuries afterward.
tutorNotes.commonErrors: Learners often confuse «consejo» (advice, a piece of guidance) with «consejero» (advisor, the person who gives it), and mistake the closing verse of each exemplo for ordinary dialogue instead of recognizing it as the traditional moral that ends every tale.

question.en: What does Patronio do every time Count Lucanor asks him for advice?
question.es: ¿Qué hace Patronio cada vez que el Conde Lucanor le pide consejo?

question.en: How does the young man in the first tale treat his wife on their wedding night, and why?
question.es: ¿Cómo trata el mancebo a su esposa en el primer cuento durante la noche de bodas, y por qué?

question.en: What trick does the fox use to get the crow's cheese?
question.es: ¿Qué truco usa la zorra para conseguir el queso del cuervo?

question.en: What do the swindlers claim is special about the cloth they pretend to be weaving?
question.es: ¿Qué afirman los burladores que tiene de especial el paño que fingen estar tejiendo?

question.en: What do all three stories suggest about why people let themselves be fooled or controlled?
question.es: ¿Qué sugieren los tres cuentos sobre por qué las personas se dejan engañar o controlar?
